slides.title: Course foundation and prior work
slides.subtitle: Use established feature extraction, then test one modest extension
slides.callout: No claim of a new backbone or an unprecedented combination. Novelty remains limited.
slides.notes: Lecture 8 part 2 page 9 distinguishes local/global features; our crop is a regional descriptor, not a keypoint. Lecture 14 part 2 pp 2-3 and 27 cover extractor/classifier and softmax. MobileNetV2 is our architecture choice, not claimed taught by name. Sources: https://lear.inrialpes.fr/people/triggs/pubs/Dalal-cvpr05.pdf ; https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04381 ; https://github.com/AtanuCSE/CricketShotDetection ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.09187 . Do not compare published percentages across datasets.

slides.title: Evaluation choices and their limits
slides.subtitle: All five methods share images, labels, visual groups and split identities

rows: No new split or seed search

slides.callout: Exploratory: grouping changed after preliminary evaluation; HOG was added after old results were known.
slides.notes: One validation set was reused for regularization, calibration and threshold selection. This can overfit validation. We disclose it rather than create a new split and pretend the original test was untouched. Initial hash-only contrast result was 96.3%; stronger transformed-copy grouping yields 65.5%. Both results and original individual predictions remain available.

slides.title: Implemented pipeline
slides.subtitle: Only the small cricket classifiers learn from the training images
slides.callout: The fixed crop is a regional view. It does not detect or segment the batter.
slides.notes: Explain the two branches. HOG and CNN global inputs have identical aspect-preserving 224 square geometry. CNN has two view passes; its global, crop and fused heads share features. HOG uses luminance, unsigned gradients, cells, blocks and per-image normalization. No StandardScaler or PCA learns from test. Source: actual implemented pipeline; lecture mapping in docs/course_mapping.md.

slides.title: HOG: gradients, cells and blocks
slides.subtitle: Lecture 10: accumulate gradient magnitude in orientation bins
slides.callout: Votes use magnitude, not frequency. No learned feature scaling; no test-based HOG tuning.
slides.notes: Trace gx and gy central differences, sqrt(gx²+gy²), atan2 modulo 180. A 50-degree gradient of magnitude 90 votes 45 to the 40-degree bin and 45 to 60. No spatial vote interpolation. Each 36-value block divides by sqrt(sum(h²)+1e-10). 13*13*36=6084. This is a documented HOG variant, not the exact signed-angle lecture example or original pedestrian detector. Lecture 10 pp 7-23; original method https://lear.inrialpes.fr/people/triggs/pubs/Dalal-cvpr05.pdf .

slides.title: CNN views and the contrast feature
slides.subtitle: Frozen ImageNet MobileNetV2 gives two 1,280-value pooled embeddings

blocks.text:
Absolute difference is nonlinear; signed difference would be redundant
for a linear head on concatenation. This motivates a test, not a success claim.

slides.notes: Both vectors are normalized before joining; the joined descriptor is normalized again. Contrast W has (4,3840) shape plus four biases. It learns weighted multiclass cross-entropy with L2 regularization. No bat-motion interpretation is assigned to feature coordinates. Actual inputs are displayed in the demo. MobileNetV2: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04381 ; ONNX weights: https://github.com/onnx/models .

slides.title: Recognition results
slides.subtitle: Same corrected split; every test image contributes, including review cases
slides.callout: HOG is a controlled baseline. Pretrained features help here; contrast adds only three correct images.
slides.notes: HOG fixed settings, validation-selected C and predictions are saved under results/hog. Do not try a new descriptor after seeing the 35.3% test score to improve a headline. CNN heads/predictions are retained unchanged. This comparison does not isolate color versus pretraining versus architecture; no general statement that all HOG methods are inferior. Evidence: results/revision/comparison.csv and saved individual probabilities.

slides.title: Uncertainty comes from 70 visual groups
slides.subtitle: Whole-group bootstrap, 2,000 paired draws, fixed model and split
slides.callout: Contrast minus concatenation: +0.32 points; interval -1.46 to +2.38. No clear advantage.
slides.notes: Draw groups with replacement and keep all images within each drawn group. Reuse draws between methods for paired differences. Statistics are image-weighted in each resample. Intervals omit training/split variability and unknown match correlation. They are not a hypothesis-test certificate of equality. Contrast 619/945, concatenation 616/945. Data and calculations: scripts/analyze_revision.py.

slides.title: Class errors
slides.subtitle: Contrast confusion counts; rows are dataset labels
slides.callout: Macro F1 averages the four class F1 scores equally. Review does not remove mistakes from this table.
slides.notes: Read an off-diagonal entry and explain precision versus recall. Glance/flick is difficult under this protocol. HOG predicts pull for 110 of 224 sweep images. Fixed geometry, similar stances and background are plausible issues, not proven causes for each error. Evidence: saved prediction arithmetic in comparison.json.

slides.title: Scores, calibration and secondary review
slides.subtitle: Temperature scaling worsened the recorded test calibration

blocks.text:
557 / 945 accepted
433 accepted predictions correct
58.9% coverage / 77.7% accuracy

Keep T = 0.802 and threshold = 0.70 unchanged.
The 90% validation target did not transfer to test.

slides.callout: Softmax is a relative class score. Agreement is not a guarantee or an unknown-shot detector.
slides.notes: NLL and ECE worsen; do not say calibration improved. ECE uses ten equal-width confidence bins. The same validation set selected C, temperature and threshold. The gate needs global/crop/contrast agreement; the heads are correlated. HOG scores are unscaled and do not affect review. Sources: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/guo17a.html ; https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.08500 .

slides.title: A confident error stays in the demo
slides.subtitle: Selected after evaluation, alongside successful and disagreement examples
slides.callout: Inspect the upstream label, predicted label and actual input views. Confidence can be wrong.
slides.notes: Use image_04199, the preserved confident failure. Do not invent its exact cause or silently relabel it. The selected picture is an illustration, not an estimate of failure frequency. Real data source: aneesh10/cricket-shot-dataset v2. Follow with the view-disagreement image_00014.

slides.title: What we can defend
slides.subtitle: An implemented comparison with useful negative findings

blocks.text: HOG and frozen features, each followed by a trained multiclass head.

Contrast gains three test images; uncertainty spans no gain.
The audit corrects optimism, and calibration fails to transfer.

slides.callout: Next useful step: independently labeled data with known match and player identities.
slides.notes: Novelty remains a weakness, not a promise of marks. Do not claim a new architecture, detector or state-of-the-art result. Mention unknown upstream license, possible missed copies and unverified labels. Course mapping and viva guide contain actual page references and a tensor-shape trace. Team identities and the real repository URL are on the cover; assistance is attributed.

Image audit: hashes, transforms, ORB/RANSAC links; all connected copies stay together.

slides.notes: Use only for questions. Equal 30.2% majority accuracy means weak video recognition, despite higher macro F1. Fixed crop followed pilot test feedback. Source: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/amittalmale/cricket-shots . Image audit: pHash <=6 bits with thumbnail MAD, rotations/mirrors, then 15 feature neighbors within cosine .20. ORB binary matching, .72 ratio, >=16 matches, >=12 RANSAC inliers, >=65% inlier fraction, >=8% hull coverage. These are evaluation tools, not a novel shot classifier. Other sources: https://github.com/onnx/models ; https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn ; https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime ; https://github.com/opencv/opencv ; https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.00859 . Full URLs, saved evidence and complete code appendix accompany the report.
